notes.summary: Exact finite rational-carrier projection for continuous real-PA PC perturbations: rational matching and recession equations plus ambient supports on ENTIRE original incident cells. S306 hypotheses and coarse propagation checked; no free attachment or uniform refinement constant.
notes.detailedSummary: On every finite common rational refinement of the original finite embedded positive-balanced complex and the actual PA reference, bounded affine matching tuples form a rational linear space. Explicit point/ray support rows project exactly to its continuous-PC tuples. One ambient support is required for each original face and each carrier cell within it, on every entire original incident top cell. Qualified S306 supplies necessity on a carrying refinement; convexity propagates its support back to coarse original cells. Local supports imply every legal PCC on every structure. Genuine finite real scalar membership and equivalence with source local-cycle PA positivity are independently proved. The resulting projections are nonempty and form a directed convex family. This is a mathematical proof, not a finite test of all carriers.
notes.text:
Fix the original category: X=|Π|⊂N⊗R is the support of a finite pure rational complex retaining all closed faces. Tangent lattices Nσ=N∩span(σ−σ) are saturated. Actual top weights are positive and satisfy the inward primitive normal balancing equation at EVERY facet, with no omitted boundary. Formal BMPS weights are rational; the explicitly qualified positive-real balancing extension also satisfies this proof's hypotheses. The actual reference γ is continuous PC, finite PA on a rational carrier and strictly positive on each nonzero cell recession direction. Literal PA has integral tangent slopes and rational constants; real PA is its finite real scalar extension on a common rational carrier. No arbitrary irrational switching walls are allowed.

A printed PCC has rational endpoints xi, real nonnegative αi summing to one, center y=Σαixi, and faces τ≼σi in some rational structure, y∈τ, xi∈σi. Centers can be irrational. PC means all its Jensen inequalities. Set B=C_b(X), J_P(h)=h(y)−Σαih(xi), b_P=Σαiγ(xi)−γ(y)≥0, and K={h∈B:J_P(h)≤b_P for every legal P}. Thus γ+K is the continuous bounded-relative PC class, without invoking automatic continuity of raw PC.

Finite geometry used below has elementary proofs. A finite cone is closed: eliminate active dependent columns by subtracting a relation until the remaining columns are independent; each inverse column map bounds coefficients by a fixed multiple of the represented vector norm. A convergent represented sequence has a subsequence on one independent list with convergent bounded coefficients. A rational inequality cone has rational lineality; after removing it, the sum of its defining nonnegative forms has a bounded level-one section. A nonvertex in a bounded polyhedron moves in both signs of an active-kernel direction until an additional independent row becomes active; induction expresses it in the finite vertex hull. Homogenization gives P=conv V+cone R with rational point/ray lists. For pointed P choose extreme homogenized rays; positive-height ones normalize to vertices, since a segment decomposition would contradict extremality. Fourier–Motzkin elimination, pairing each lower and upper bound on a variable, proves exact finite projections. Rational hyperplane arrangements give common refinements.

Matching affine tuples on a rational carrier satisfy rational homogeneous equations, obtained by testing equality on rational affine bases of common faces. Gaussian elimination supplies a rational basis; clearing its finitely many tangent-slope denominators makes each basis tuple literal PA. Their real span is exactly genuine real PA on that carrier. Boundedness adds rational equations setting all recession slopes to zero. For c=conv Vc+cone Rc, a bounded affine function has value a convex combination of its values at Vc; therefore its uniform norm is the maximum absolute value over these finitely many rational point generators.

Continuous printed PC extends to real-endpoint PCCs. Introduce perspective variables ti=αixi. Cell inequalities Aixi≤bi become Aiti≤αibi, together with αi≥0, sum-one and Σti∈τ. This is a rational polyhedron. At any feasible configuration, impose active rows as equalities; rational Gaussian elimination and approximation in its rational kernel retain all inactive strict slacks and positive coefficients. The resulting rational endpoints ti/αi and rational centers give printed tests. Continuity passes to the given real configuration. In particular f is convex on each ENTIRE original cell.

A continuous function having one ambient affine local lower support at every point satisfies all printed PCCs on all structures. On any contained segment local supports give local midpoint inequalities. Subtract the endpoint chord. If the difference q is positive internally, q(t)+εt², for sufficiently small ε>0, has an interior maximum. The local midpoint inequality at that point makes the mean at nearby symmetric arguments exceed the maximum by εs², a contradiction. Thus the segment restriction is convex. Its initial supporting slope bounds the full endpoint secant. At a PCC center sum those endpoint bounds using the SAME ambient support; the linear terms cancel. This proves the assertion even for irrational centers and distant endpoints.

For each finite rational common refinement C of Π and the actual reference carrier, compute the bounded matching space W_C with rational basis φ1,…,φm; write h=Σzjφj. For EACH original face τ and EACH carrier cell ρ⊂τ introduce ambient affine sτρ(x)=pτρ(x)+eτρ. Require equality with γ+h on every point and recession generator of ρ. For EVERY original top cell σ≽τ and EVERY carrier cell c⊂σ require sτρ(v)≤γ(v)+Σzjφj(v) for v∈Vc, and pτρ(r)≤γc,lin(r) for r∈Rc. Recession perturbation slopes vanish. Turn equalities into paired inequalities and list support coordinates as u. The result is A_C z+N_C u≤d_C. A_C,N_C are rational, while d_C contains the ACTUAL real reference values/slopes. Original top faces are included among τ. These explicit finite rows use no PC oracle or non-PA target.

The projection is EXACTLY K∩W_C. Sufficiency follows because generator equalities hold on all of ρ and generator inequalities on every ENTIRE incident original cell. Every real face point belongs to a carrier cell, so it has a common ambient support; the segment argument proves all PCCs. Necessity uses precisely qualified S306: f=γ+h is continuous finite printed-PC, bounded relative to actual cellwise-affine real γ, on a finite pure globally embedded rational refinement, positive weights balanced at every facet, all closed faces retained. Refinement preserves balance: new interior facets have equal inherited weights and opposite saturated normals, and subdivided old facets retain the old relation. S306 gives a support at each point on entire incident REFINED cells; no refinement-uniform constant is assumed. At y∈relint ρ, the segment to any point of an original incident σ initially lies in a refined incident cell. Its supporting bound propagates to the distant endpoint by convexity on the entire original σ, even if γ was not affine on coarse σ. Since f is affine on ρ, both tangent signs force the support to agree on its entire affine hull. It solves all required rows. Finitely many choices supply u. Zero is feasible because γ is PC. Common refinements preserve represented values; the union of these projections is directed and convex and is exactly the real-PA PC perturbation class.

This PA PC class agrees with BMPS local-cycle positivity in the stated relative domain. For the forward direction subtract the S306 ambient support from the primitive tangent-corrected coefficient Σcσfσ(nσ/τ)−fτ(Σcσnσ/τ). Tangent equality and balancing cancel the support, leaving nonnegative inward residuals against every nonnegative local cycle, in every dimension. Conversely at rational y choose rational incident tangent generators vj with derivative costs cj. Every rational nonnegative zero relation Σλjvj=0 is a rational balanced local one-cycle after primitive rescaling and coincident-ray merging. Positivity gives Σλjcj≥0. The relation cone is rational finitely generated, so this holds for all real zero relations. The closed finite cone generated by (vj,cj),(0,1) excludes (0,−1). Nearest-point separation has strictly positive vertical coefficient, yielding p(vj)≤cj. It is a common local support. Tangent cones and costs are unchanged within a carrier-face relative interior, so that support applies to every real point there. The segment argument proves printed PC. No source automatic-continuity theorem or real-domain density theorem is imported.

Separation foundation for n2 is also explicit. A linear functional dominated by sublinear p extends across a vector v by choosing its value in [sup_u(f(u)−p(u−v)), inf_u(p(u+v)−f(u))]; subadditivity orders these bounds. Zorn's lemma extends it globally. For a closed convex cone D and z outside it in a Hausdorff locally convex space choose balanced open U with z∉D+U. The open convex absorbing set O=D+U has finite sublinear gauge p and O={p<1}. Extend f(az)=a p(z) dominated by p. Bounds on a balanced neighborhood give continuity; scaling D gives f(D)≤0<f(z). For a closed convex normed-space set L containing zero use O=L+ε open ball with ε<dist(z,L). The same extension gives f(z)≥1 and f(l)≤1−ε||f||, a finite strict separating bound. This proves the needed separation forms without an external LP or duality grant.

Complete proofs and explicit row conventions are in P05.1-paper.tex §§2–4 and author PDF. Rerun metadata with python build_artifacts.py. This note uses only the exact qualified S306 assertions stated above, not its missing cited dependencies. No MA, contact, or universal real density conclusion is asserted here.

notes.summary: Independent costed weak-star Farkas theorem in the FULL C_b dual, exact carrier multipliers, and explicit all-carrier criterion equivalent to continuous-PC real-PA density. Slack, infinity and zero-scale separators retained.
notes.detailedSummary: Dγ is the weak-star/product closed cone of costed PCC generators (J_P,b_P) and (0,1). It equals all valid inequalities ℓ(h)≤t on K, proved by locally convex separation with separate positive-scale and zero-scale cases. Each n1 carrier projection has exact finite multiplier equations Aᵀλ=a_C(ℓ), Nᵀλ=0, dᵀλ≤t. The geometry-only implication that multipliers on EVERY carrier force (ℓ,t)∈Dγ is necessary and sufficient for norm density. It contains no envelope or assumed approximation condition. The full Banach dual and nets are essential; no Radon-measure restriction or refinement-uniform constant is imposed. This independently proves the proposed ROOT315 reduction, which remains unreviewed data.
notes.text:
Use n1's exact category, K, J_P,b_P≥0 and explicit finite carrier systems A_C z+N_C u≤d_C with rational bounded matching basis φ_C,j. Let B*=the FULL Banach dual of B=C_b(X), and a_C(ℓ)j=ℓ(φ_C,j). Define Dγ as the closure of cone{(J_P,b_P),(0,1):P legal} in σ(B*,B)×the usual real topology. Closure allows nets; costs are not homogenized away.

Costed Farkas: (ℓ,t)∈Dγ iff ℓ(h)≤t for every h∈K. Validity follows on generators, positive sums and weak-star/product limits by testing fixed h. Conversely n1's separation applied to an outside point gives a continuous pairing η(h)−rs with ℓ(h)−ts>0, J_P(h)−b_Ps≤0 for every P, and s≥0. Every weak-star-continuous linear functional is a finite linear combination of evaluations on B*: continuity bounds it by finitely many evaluations, so it vanishes on their joint kernel and factors through their finite-dimensional image. Thus the stated pairing is the entire continuous dual. If s>0, h/s∈K violates validity. If s=0, J_P(h)≤0 and nh∈K for every n≥0 because b_P≥0; validity forces ℓ(h)≤0, contradicting separation. No Slater hypothesis is needed.

The full B* includes behavior at infinity. On the subspace of bounded continuous functions on R having a limit at +∞, evaluation of that limit has norm one. The dominated-extension construction in n1 extends it to C_b(R), annihilating C_0(R) and taking 1 to 1. It cannot be a finite signed Radon measure on R: vanishing on compact continuous tests forces such a measure to vanish, while its total mass would be one. No representation theorem is used in the criterion. In a nonseparable predual no sequential closure is substituted for weak-star closure.

Slack matters even on the balanced line γ=|x|. The PCC of −1,1 centered at zero has b=1. The valid convex relative target f=|x|+(1−|x|)_+/2 has perturbation J_P(f−γ)=1/2. Dropping b and imposing J_P(h)≤0 would exclude it. Any homogenization must retain the cost coordinate and fixed slice.

Finite multiplier theorem: ℓ(h)≤t on K∩W_C iff some finite λ≥0 satisfies A_Cᵀλ=a_C(ℓ), N_Cᵀλ=0, d_Cᵀλ≤t. Multiplication proves sufficiency. For necessity form the finite closed cone generated by (A_i,N_i,d_i),(0,0,1). If (a_C(ℓ),0,t) is outside it, finite cone separation gives (z,u,s), s≥0, A_i z+N_i u≤d_i s and a_C(ℓ)·z−ts>0. For s>0 divide to obtain a feasible violation. For s=0 add n(z,u) to an existing feasible tuple; n1 guarantees one because γ itself is PC. This violates the bound for large n. Both are impossible. Cone membership gives the multipliers with the vertical generator absorbing t−dᵀλ. Actual irrational right sides, unbounded support variables and non-strict feasibility cause no gap.

Explicit pair criterion C(X,γ): for every ℓ∈B* and t∈R, if for EVERY finite common rational carrier C there exists λ_C≥0 satisfying the preceding three finite equations/inequality, then (ℓ,t)∈Dγ. Its statement uses only original rational point/ray and incidence data, coefficient lattice/matching matrices, actual γ, legal PCC evaluations and specified bounded linear dual data. It contains no desired envelope, target approximation, density or presumed feasibility for a non-PA function.

Proof of equivalence to continuous relative-PC density: let L be the norm closure of the directed convex union of n1 projections K∩W_C. It is closed convex, contains zero and lies in K. By finite multipliers the criterion's premise is precisely validity on L; by costed Farkas its conclusion is validity on K. If L=K the implication holds. If h0∈K∖L, n1's norm separation gives ℓ,t with ℓ|L≤t<ℓ(h0), violating the implication. Thus C(X,γ) iff L=K. The proof uses density to identify the reduction, but the CONDITION itself has been fully eliminated to the explicit geometric/linear data. This is not the assertion that an operator is dense exactly when it is dense.

These are infinite certificates, not a finite algorithm. The continuum claims are proofs, not consequences of the finite checker. P05.1-paper.tex §5 gives the full arguments; build with pdflatex -no-shell-escape -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error P05.1-paper.tex. ROOT315 is independently reconstructed mathematical data, never a support ID. No MA construction follows from this note.

notes.summary: New rational interpolation bridge: original finite genuine REAL-PA obstacles, continuous-PC density, the explicit dual criterion, and ALL C_b envelope regularity are equivalent. Strict decreasing common shifts proved without PC roof gluing.
notes.detailedSummary: S306 single-cell roofs bound a compatible generalized-simplex nodal/recession interpolant q with f≤q≤f+η. The interpolant is genuine finite rational-carrier real PA and need not be PC; it is used as an obstacle, so shared support gluing of the roofs is unnecessary. Qualified R230 identifies the actual unrestricted all-C_b envelope first. Both directions of the original PA-obstacle/density/all-obstacle bridge then follow, including nonseparable obstacles. Rational common shifts give strictly decreasing uniform PA-PC sequences with one bounded relative family and actual reference recession. Every S306 application uses the continuous target, actual reference, whole-cell Lipschitz, strict recession and all-face balancing hypotheses.
notes.text:
Work in n1's exact real-reference category. For each continuous PC f bounded relative to the ACTUAL γ and each η>0, we prove a compatible finite genuine real-PA q, not asserted PC, with f≤q≤f+η on the ENTIRE support and q−γ bounded real PA.

First refine so γ is affine on every top cell σ. All closed faces and all facet balancing are retained. Qualified S306's global CLOSED-CELL Lipschitz theorem applies: f continuous finite printed-PC, |f−γ| bounded, actual real cellwise-affine γ, finite pure globally embedded rational complex and actual strictly positive weights balanced at every facet. It gives finite global cellwise Lipschitz bounds, not ambient-distance bounds across nonincident components. n1's perspective argument gives convexity on each entire σ. The actual affine γσ is positive on every nonzero rec σ direction. Thus S306's ONE-CELL theorem has every hypothesis: continuous convex finite fσ, bounded difference from actual affine reference, explicit global cell Lipschitz constant and strict actual recession. It produces a finite convex rational-spatial real-PA roof pσ with f≤pσ≤f+η and exact reference recession. Independent roofs are not presumed to match or to glue PC.

Construct a common compatible rational generalized-simplex subdivision refining all their spatial carriers. Homogenize all rational cell inequalities in V×R, include s=0 and coordinate hyperplanes. The central rational arrangement has pointed cones because each lies in a coordinate orthant. It refines all homogenized cells, including their faces at s=0. For each nonzero face choose a rational interior ray. Inductively cone from it to the already triangulated boundary; in a bounded positive-form section this covers the polytope and meets along common faces. Shared faces use the same chosen ray. Flag generators are independent because an interior ray is outside the span of a previous proper face. Normalize positive-s generators to (vi,1) and keep zero-s generators (rj,0). The s=1 sections are c=conv{vi}+cone{rj} with these augmented vectors independent. This is a finite compatible subdivision, also of recession geometry.

On such c⊂σ define the unique affine q by q(vi)=f(vi) and q_lin(rj)=γσ,lin(rj). Shared finite faces have identical vertex values and reference recession slopes, so the formulas match on their entire point/ray representations. Disjoint actual cells sharing a direction at infinity do not identify their ray heights; their reference slopes may differ there. Rational matching, as proved in n1, makes q a GENUINE finite real scalar extension on this rational carrier. Actual heights are not rounded and irrational comparison walls are not introduced.

For convex f on σ with upper bound γσ+C, every feasible recession ray satisfies f(x+r)≤f(x)+γσ,lin(r): a larger unit secant would persist on all longer secants by convexity, violating the affine upper bound. Therefore for x=Σαivi+Σβjrj, αi,βj≥0, Σαi=1, convexity and repeated recession bounds give f(x)≤q(x). The roof pσ is affine on c with the same ray slopes, so q(x)−pσ(x)=Σαi(f(vi)−pσ(vi))≤0. Hence f≤q≤pσ≤f+η everywhere. In particular q−γ is bounded genuine real PA. This construction uses no PC gluing assertion for q or the roofs.

The ACTUAL envelope is Eγ(u)=sup{a:a finite printed-PC, a≤γ+u, a≤γ+C_a globally}. Competitors may be discontinuous and have only upper growth. Qualified R230 applies on this positive all-face-balanced finite embedded support, continuous PC γ and ANY u∈C_b(X). It proves Eγ(u) continuous PC, identifies it with the continuous-competitor envelope, and gives γ+inf u≤Eγ(u)≤γ+u≤γ+sup u. This is used BEFORE density, with no separability or PA obstacle hypothesis. It does not itself give PA density.

By n2, criterion C(X,γ) is equivalent to continuous relative-PC real-PA-PC density. Density applies to that actual continuous bounded-relative envelope, proving regularity for EVERY C_b obstacle and hence every bounded genuine real-PA obstacle. Conversely assume original regularity for every bounded genuine real-PA obstacle. Given continuous relative-PC f, use the constructed q and legal obstacle u=q−γ. The function f is itself admissible, so f≤Eγ(u)≤q≤f+η. Approximate this regularizable endpoint by real-PA PC within η and let η↓0; a diagonal choice gives density of f. No matrix feasibility was inferred from continuous completion. A direct converse from the all-C_b property takes u=f−γ, whose actual envelope is f. Thus the original PA-obstacle property, all-C_b property, continuous density and n2 criterion are exactly equivalent, including arbitrary nonseparable obstacles.

Strict decrease is proved in the true category. Choose PA-PC a_n with ||a_n−e||∞≤δ_n=2^−n, n≥1. Set g_n=a_n+5δ_n. Rational common constants are literal PA and hence belong to the genuine real extension. Errors satisfy 4δ_n≤g_n−e≤6δ_n and g_n−g_(n+1)≥4δ_n−6δ_(n+1)=δ_n>0. The sequences converge uniformly and have one relative bound ||e−γ||∞+3. Bounded differences preserve actual recession on every feasible ray. Each term has a finite rational carrier; no common FINITE carrier for the infinite sequence is asserted. The functions a_n−δ_n are admissible PA competitors below e with error at most 2δ_n, proving equality with their supremum. These shifts need not retain contacts; no irrational-wall maximum is used.

Complete construction and bridge proofs are in P05.1-paper.tex §6. Source/application checks are in source-application-ledger.md and proof-coverage.md. This extends the dual characterization to actual unrestricted envelopes; it proves no MA extension or contact identity.

notes.summary: Reconstructed actual literal bounded obstacle and nonregularizable envelope in every admitted positive dimension; compact embedded positive-balanced branch is empty, and zero-dimensional pairs regular in both branches.
notes.detailedSummary: For an admitted literal positive-growth reference on a noncompact balanced finite support, f=(1−1/D)γ+(1/D)max(γ,A) has a nonintegral tangent slope and a positive uniform distance from all literal PA-PC functions. Integral norm cones contacting every rational vertex produce a bounded literal obstacle whose ACTUAL unrestricted envelope equals f; R230 controls discontinuous upper-only competitors. A covolume stationary-divergence proof excludes every positive-dimensional compact embedded positive-balanced support, componentwise. The whole original dossier fixes BMPS's finite globally embedded definition and supplies no atlas definition. Zero-dimensional finite rational sets have exact singleton envelopes and strict rational approximations for all C_b obstacles. No absent book-local proof is imported.
notes.text:
Use n1's ambient category and literal admitted γ. A finite PA reference strictly positive on each nonzero cell recession direction is coercive. In a point/ray representation positivity excludes lineality; choose c>0 below its finitely many positive ray-slope/norm ratios and bound finite point values below by c||v||−D. Triangle inequalities give γ(x)≥c||x||−D on each cell. Bounded cells are covered by increasing D. Finiteness gives the global estimate and compact sublevels.

For noncompact X choose an unbounded reference cell. Its integral gradient m is nonzero by positive recession. Choose primitive tangent lattice v with k=m(v)≠0, rational x0 in its relative interior, rational A>γ(x0), integer D>|k|, D≥2 and λ=1/D. Set G=max(γ,A), H=(A−γ)_+, f=(1−λ)γ+λG and δ=f−γ=λH. The maximum is literal PA on rational walls and PC directly by Jensen; f is rational-affine continuous PC, genuine real PA and bounded relative to γ. H is bounded, compactly supported. Near x0 below level A, f has slope a=k−k/D∉Z on v. Choose rational r>0 with x0+tv, |t|≤r, remaining there. Any literal PA-PC g is convex on this segment by n1. At a differentiability point t∈[−r/2,r/2] its derivative is integral, since v belongs to the tangent lattice of its active piece. If uniform error is e, convex secants to −r and r give a−4e/r≤g′(t)≤a+4e/r. Therefore e≥r dist(a,Z)/4>0, independently of its carrier refinement.

Construct an actual admissible literal obstacle, rather than merely a density obstruction. Refine the common rational carrier of γ,G,f,H by coordinate orthants to make cells pointed, and let S be the finite union of all rational vertices. δ(s) is rational. For an ambient integral polyhedral norm ρ there is an integer M>0 with δ(x)≤δ(s)+Mρ(x−s) for every x∈X,s∈S. On a carrier cell containing s its finite affine gradient bounds the ratio. Every other closed cell avoids a positive neighborhood of s; bounded δ controls the ratio there. Finite lists and norm equivalence give one M; no ambient Lipschitz theorem across components is assumed. Define u=min{H, min_s[δ(s)+Mρ(x−s)]}. All slopes are integral, constants rational and comparison walls rational, so u is literal PA on a finite rational carrier. It is continuous bounded, 0≤u≤H, u≥δ and u(s)=δ(s). It vanishes outside a compact set.

The function f is an admissible competitor for obstacle γ+u. For ANY original upper-only possibly discontinuous competitor q, R230 applies under positive all-face balancing and supplies its continuous PC completion F≥q, agreeing at rational points and staying below γ+u and γ+C_q by dense rational comparison. Thus F(s)≤f(s) at every vertex. On each carrier cell γ and f are affine with the same recession slope. Convexity and upper growth imply F(x+r)≤F(x)+γ_lin(r) as in n3. A pointed cell is its rational vertex hull plus recession cone, so for EVERY real x=Σαis_i+Σβjrj, F(x)≤Σαif(s_i)+Σβjf_lin(rj)=f(x). Hence all original q≤f and the ACTUAL envelope is exactly f. The positive arithmetic error floor proves literal nonregularizability.

Concrete instance: X=R, γ=|x|, A=1, λ=1/2, f=|x|+(1−|x|)_+/2. Take u(x)=1/2+|x| for |x|≤1/4, u(x)=1−|x| for 1/4≤|x|≤1, and u=0 outside. Its slopes are integral and constants/breakpoints rational. Its actual envelope is f. Around x=1/2 with radius 1/4 the endpoint slope is 1/2, yielding the explicit error floor 1/32, not claimed sharp.

Compactness is not assumed away. Qualified B225 gives finite embedded noncompactness; here is its independent proof. Let aσ be the Euclidean covolume of the saturated tangent lattice, νσ/τ the inward unit conormal. A facet lattice basis plus its primitive inward lift is a top lattice basis, so perpendicular height is aσ/aτ. Balancing gives Σwσaσνσ/τ=0. The ordinary polyhedral divergence formula, with unbounded cells truncated beyond a compactly supported vector field, implies Σwσaσ∫σdivσY=0 because facet fluxes cancel. If X were compact and dimension d>0, choose Y(x)=x near it. This would yield 0=dΣwσaσvol_d(σ)>0. Thus no such compact support exists. Finite connected components retain all incident balancing equations and each positive-dimensional component is noncompact. Bounded skeletons need not be balanced at their boundary.

The original-scope decision uses the WHOLE dossier, not an extra hypothesis: its problem asks BMPS balanced rational spaces, says it uses arXiv v1 throughout, and supplies no atlas definition or transition data. BMPS Definitions2.2/2.4/2.27 explicitly specify finite complexes, X⊂one N_R, and a strictly positive pure top cycle. Thus the original compact positive-dimensional literal residual has no instances under its stated definition. Compact charted spaces or toric compactifications are different categories. B225/R230's chart assertions retain their compatible local hypotheses and finite bounded rational decomposition requirement for literal PA; arbitrary charts are not imported here.

In dimension zero X is a finite set of rational singleton faces. Every PCC is trivial, so Eγ(u)=γ+u pointwise. Real PA is every function on this finite set. Literal PA takes rational values; for any C_b obstacle choose rational a_n within δ_n=2^−n at every point and add common rational 5δ_n. Errors [4δ_n,6δ_n] give strict descent as in n3. Literal obstacles already have exact literal endpoints. Empty supports are vacuous and positive-at-infinity is vacuous in dimension zero.

notes.text:
Complete solution CLAIM for original P05.1, under its exact stated BMPS definition: (i) every zero-dimensional pair is regular in both the literal and genuine finite real scalar branches, also for all C_b obstacles; (ii) every positive-dimensional admitted literal pair fails, with n4's actual bounded literal obstacle and exact nonregularizable envelope; (iii) for every admitted actual real reference, regularity is equivalent to n2's explicit criterion C(X,γ). By n3 the equivalence holds both for the ORIGINAL bounded genuine real-PA obstacle class and for EVERY bounded continuous obstacle, including nonseparable ones. The compact positive-dimensional source branch is empty by n4. This is a complete coefficient-separated characterization by the expressly permitted infinite geometric/linear certificate. The final candidate flag is true as an author mathematical claim, not mathematical acceptance.

The certificate is solely specified original rational cells and lattice/matching data, ACTUAL γ, costed legal PCC evaluations and FULL bounded linear dual data: for all (ℓ,t), finite nonnegative multipliers satisfying A_Cᵀλ_C=a_C(ℓ), N_Cᵀλ_C=0, d_Cᵀλ_C≤t on EVERY finite common rational carrier must imply (ℓ,t) lies in the weak-star/product closed cone of (J_P,b_P),(0,1). n1 proves exact projections on every carrier; n2 proves costed Farkas and the finite multiplier theorem; n3 proves the actual-envelope bridge. There is no density or desired envelope property assumed in the criterion's statement.

An actual bad-pair certificate consists of ℓ,t, all those carrier multipliers, and specified h∈C_b(X) satisfying J_P(h)≤b_P on every legal PCC and ℓ(h)>t. Then every real-PA PC a in the actual growth class satisfies ||a−(γ+h)||∞≥(ℓ(h)−t)/||ℓ||>0.
